title: Planner: private tasks stored in your private plan instead of Microsoft To Do
summary: Hold: the cited PowerShell reference describes the printed command as unblocking an app, not blocking it. The briefing also treats private-plan eDiscovery as undocumented despite Microsoft's published exclusion of non-group plans. The rollout dates and automatic deployment match Microsoft's notice.

claims.claim: New private tasks created in Planner and Planner-powered experiences will be stored in the user's private Planner plan instead of the Microsoft To Do task store.
claims.quote: Beginning in December 2026, private tasks created in Planner and Planner-powered experiences will be stored in a user's own private Planner plan instead of the Microsoft To Do task store.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Learn does not yet identify the precise storage backend for the new private Planner plan.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner private plan storage Azure; Planner private tasks private plan storage To Do. Opened manage-planner-app, planner-security-privacy-compliance and planner-for-admins; these describe Exchange, basic and premium storage, not the new private plan's backend.

claims.claim: Storage of new private tasks moves from To Do to the Planner platform.
claims.quote: This change aligns private task management with the Planner platform while preserving enterprise compliance and security protections.

claims.claim: Purview eDiscovery and history are supported for basic plans contained by groups.
claims.quote: Purview eDiscovery and history are supported for basic plans contained by groups.

claims.claim: Premium plans and non-group plans are not currently supported for Purview eDiscovery and history.
claims.quote: Purview eDiscovery and history are supported for basic plans contained by groups. Premium plans and non-group plans aren't currently supported.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: After rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not said how a user's private, non-shared Planner plan is treated for eDiscovery.
claims.quote: Purview eDiscovery and history are supported for basic plans contained by groups. Premium plans and non-group plans aren't currently supported.
claims.fix: Replace 'It does not say how a private plan is treated, which is the point to confirm for eDiscovery of new private tasks.' with 'Microsoft documents no current Purview eDiscovery and history support for non-group plans.' In What's changing, replace 'Learn does not yet describe the private plan storage, so what the change does to storage, discovery and retention is known only from the roadmap item and the notice.' with 'Learn does not yet identify the precise storage backend for the new private plan.' In After rollout, remove the reason 'because Learn's Planner security page does not say how private plans are treated'. Remove eDiscovery and content search from the first Open questions bullet rather than presenting their support for a non-group plan as undocumented. Keep the existing source https://learn.microsoft.com/planner/planner-security-privacy-compliance.

claims.claim: The Planner security page says retention policy is not currently supported.
claims.quote: Retention policy isn't currently supported.

claims.quote: Users with a Microsoft 365 license are entitled to the Planner app.

claims.claim: Included is the licensing model for this change inside the licensed Planner product.
claims.quote: Users with a qualifying Microsoft 365 license have access to a rich set of capabilities for individual and team work management. These include basic plan creation and editing capabilities, task creation and editing capabilities

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A licence requirement specific to the private-task storage change has not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner private tasks license pricing; Planner private plan private tasks licensing price meter. Opened Planner for admins and manage-planner-app; read Planner service-description licensing excerpts. No licence specific to the storage change was stated.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No meter specific to this private-task storage change is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner private plan private tasks licensing price meter. Opened Planner for admins and manage-planner-app; read service-description entitlements, including its general Graph metering caveat. No meter for this storage change was stated.

claims.claim: No price specific to the storage change has been published.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner private tasks license pricing; Planner private plan private tasks licensing price meter. Opened Planner for admins and manage-planner-app and read service-description results. No price for the private-task storage change was stated.

claims.claim: The Planner app in Teams displays Private Tasks under My Tasks.
claims.quote:
My Tasks: This view includes:
- Private Tasks: A dedicated place for the user to quickly create tasks in a default place.

claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe the Teams-specific presentation of this storage change.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner private plan new private tasks Teams My Tasks experience December 2026. Opened manage-planner-app and Planner for admins. They describe the existing My Tasks view but not how this storage update will appear in Teams.

claims.claim: Neither an admin UI nor an API switch to keep new Planner private tasks in the To Do store is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner private tasks private plan storage To Do administrator opt out Set-PlannerConfiguration; Planner keep To Do private storage setting. Opened manage-planner-app, disable-planner and Planner for admins. No storage-selection UI or API setting was found.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Planner > Block turns off the Planner app for the organisation in Teams.
claims.quote:
In the left pane of the Teams admin center, go to Teams apps > Manage apps.

To turn off Planner for your organization, search for the Planner app, select it, and then select Block.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <Teams app ID> -IsBlocked $true is documented as blocking the Planner app in Teams.
claims.quote:
Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true

Unblocks Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b).
claims.fix: Remove the printed PowerShell call and set controls[1].api to null; retain the verified UI Block path. Add to the row note: 'The PowerShell reference labels its -IsBlocked $true example as unblocking an app, so the blocking call is not verified.' Do not reverse the Boolean by inference: the same reference also labels its $false example as unblocking.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; controls[1].scope; Governance controls; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The listed Teams app control governs Planner app availability in Teams at organisation scope, not the Web rollout itself.
claims.quote: Planner is enabled by default for all Teams users in your organization. You can turn off or turn on the app at the org level on the Manage apps page in the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: Blocking Planner in Teams is not documented as a way to retain private-task storage in Microsoft To Do.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner keep To Do private storage setting; Planner private tasks private plan storage To Do administrator opt out. Opened manage-planner-app and disable-planner. The Teams Block action controls app access; neither page describes reverting private-task storage.
